### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e48d8425258dff2d147ca91f13033f1ba41a5545` — the merge of head `3ca80e701710aeb613830a201aa4d1ee8083c142` into base `76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e48d8425258dff2d147ca91f13033f1ba41a5545 && git checkout e48d8425258dff2d147ca91f13033f1ba41a5545
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9 3ca80e701710aeb613830a201aa4d1ee8083c142 && git checkout -B drift-repro 76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9 && git merge --no-ff 3ca80e701710aeb613830a201aa4d1ee8083c142

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 76bf6c50d86f2894526851fb0a1c751f4074bba9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6998341844351372c560b56bc48cb065547a7551`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-definitions.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-guards.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-guard.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/subflow-notice-arming.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/save-notice-approval-round-trip.integration.test.ts, .changeset/28840-subflow-notice-arming.md + packages/spec/src/automation/save-notice-placement.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts (`FLOW_PAUSE_CAPABLE_NODE_TYPES`, the `saveNoticePlacementRefusals` wiring), packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts (`collectFlowGraphs`), docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md §7.3, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/map-node.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/loader-set.test-support.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-integration.test.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/packagedFlows.ts, packages/client/src/return-type-precision.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json, hotcrm `a5982564`

Face: `--paths` on the PR's file list derives the schema face (hit: `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`); the narrowing face floor (every non-prose path of the diff) is listed above it. Inputs: card #28840 (body, triage `6565522139`, claim `6565920206`, needs_decision report `6565979681`, seat ruling `6565992870` option A, done report `6567425898`), PR #28875 body and file list, the net diff against merge-base `00918c886c0d` (9 files, +663 −13), and the check-runs on the head, read until every run completed at 2026-11-02T02:32:57Z: 69 runs, 56 `success`, 13 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 in progress. Of the ten required contexts, nine concluded `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`) and `Lint UI` is `skipped` (no `ui/**` path in the diff); `Check Changeset` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are `success`; every `skipped` run is an opt-in or paths-filtered job.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set at registration, save door and `objectstack validate`: unchanged — right.** The diff touches no `registrationChecks` entry, not `save-notice-placement.ts`, not `flow.zod.ts`; `registerFlow` on the head still throws only out of the one checks list (engine.ts 4507). Every flow that registered at base registers on the head. Verified on the tree, not the body.
2. **Arming narrows — right, and it is the ruled posture.** `activateFlowTrigger` gains one decline (`declineOntoSuspendingSubflowNotice`) placed right after `declineOntoDisabledSubflows` and before the trigger lookup (engine.ts 3893–3901), so it sits inside the one gate every arming path crosses (boot pull, publish, `registerTrigger` at kernel:ready, the enable toggle). The gate is reached only after `resolveTriggerBinding` resolves, and the parse already refuses a `save_notice` in any flow whose start is not a create/update record trigger, so the only flows this decline can touch are record-triggered create/update flows. Matches ruling A ("not armed", never "refused at registration").
3. **Public surface widens — right in substance, under-declared (see ②).** `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` gains `notice_after_suspending_subflow`; the derived `FlowUnboundCause` union widens; `/_status` serves the value; `@objectstack/client` types the row as `FlowRuntimeState`. Consumers checked on the head: the Console reads `unboundCause` as an opaque string and renders "Not running here" for any value (`packagedFlows.ts` 97–99, its test loops the four known values but asserts nothing exhaustive); the client's type-precision test asserts `FlowUnboundCause | undefined` and does not enumerate; `engine.test.ts`, `subflow-guard-every-door.test.ts` and `time-relative-bind-status-e2e.test.ts` pin their own causes by literal. No `switch` over the union anywhere in the repo, so nothing breaks or needs the value. The spec `Eq` pin moved with it. `api-surface/contracts.json` records `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES (const)` by existence only and no `content/docs/references` page lists the values, so no generated artifact moves — consistent with Human Minimum 6; the `Type Check · source gates` run is green on the head.
4. **Own cause rather than folding into `disabled_subflow`: right.** The tuple's TSDoc gives each cause one owner and one remedy; this one's owner is the author (move the notice) or the child's publisher, not the administrator's activation switch.
5. **`subflowTargets` body: unchanged.** `subflow-guards.ts` changes only the host interface, one import and `rejudgeSubflowCallers`; the function reads the same top-level `subflow`/`map` `config.flowName` as before (map's config key is `flowName`, `map-node.ts` 113/126). The existing guards (`packagedSubflowCallers`, `disabledPackagedSubflows`, the §7.3 refusals) see exactly what they saw. The new reading deliberately shares that same top-level call set, so the gate and the re-judge agree; region-nested calls stay #28846's.
6. **Load-order independence: holds.** `registerFlow` ends with `rejudgeSubflowCallers(name)` for every registration (engine.ts 4584). The new loop walks `transitiveSubflowCallers` (BFS over callers, `found` set, so it terminates on call cycles) and re-offers a caller when either it is bound and now trapped, or unbound and in `subflowNoticeDeclinedFlows`. Traced on the code: child registered after parent → parent bound, trap found → unbound and declined; child republished without the pause → parent in the declined map → re-offered, `subflowNoticeTrap` undefined → map entry deleted, armed; child republished with the pause → declined again and the warn repeats (the "said once" key is the reason string, cleared on arm); grandchild changes → the BFS reaches the top caller through the middle flow, and `suspendingNode` reads through calls with a shared `seen` set (sound, since a flow's answer does not depend on the path it was reached by). The test file pins each of these and the cycle control. The early return keeps the boot pull cheap: before any trigger binds, both maps are empty and the loop never runs; the kernel:ready `registerTrigger` pass then runs the gate once per flow with every flow in hand.
7. **Child withdrawal: no re-judge, by declared design.** `withdrawFlow` drops the caller's own entry only; a caller declined onto a child that is then removed keeps its decline (and its reason names the absent child) until the child or the caller is registered again. Conservative direction (the caller would fail at its call node if armed), louder than silence, and it matches the disabled-subflow half. Accepted, not a finding.
8. **Unregistered child = not known to suspend.** `suspendingNode` answers undefined for a flow not in `flows`, so a caller registered ahead of its child arms, as today, and is disarmed when the child arrives suspending. Correct given the parse already refuses what it can see.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-automation: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right under ruling A.** Nothing an author writes changes: no authorable key, value or default moves, and the one spec change is a value on a runtime status response. The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker are in the changeset body with both declaration lines; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (PR body and changeset) — **under-declared; should-fix.** AGENTS.md defines the line as "does this diff widen or narrow a published accept set or public surface", and this diff does both: it narrows arming and it widens the published `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` tuple and the `FlowUnboundCause` union exported from `@objectstack/spec/contracts`. The closed pair admits one arm, and `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` names the form for exactly this case: "`yes (narrowing)` included: a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing face". Precedent: the tuple's own introduction (`6422da5`) was declared `yes (widening)`, and new published error codes are graded as a widening by `check-changeset-no-major` (#16342). The correct line is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in both places. No mechanical reader's verdict moves with it (the face is narrowing either way, the level follows `Metadata-protocol: none`, the ADR-0087 arm is `narrowing` either way), which is why this is should-fix and not a FAIL.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation: `Metadata-protocol: none` with both packages `patch`** — answered yes in ② (right).
- **Dev deviation: new `FLOW_UNBOUND_CAUSES` value, no new export** — right in substance; the declaration line is the only correction (②).
- **Dev deviation: the #28806 walk repeated in the service (about 40 lines) instead of exporting spec's internal `suspendedReach`** — accepted. The order prefers an internal entry and spec has none; a new public helper would itself be a surface widening. The copy mirrors the spec walk exactly (successors-not-self, loops included, region body judged by `path[1]`, which `collectFlowGraphs` always sets to the top-level container index). Drift risk is real but bounded: both are pinned by their own tests.
- **Dev deviation: round-trip test re-pointed** — answered in ④ item 5.
- **Dev deviation: `rejudgeSubflowCallers`' "moved unedited" docblock corrected** — right, but incomplete: `describeUnboundReason` and `withdrawFlow` in `flow-definitions.ts` are also edited by this diff and their one-line docblocks still read "moved unedited". Should-fix (doc accuracy only).
- **Ruled boundaries (ruling D, the stranded-decision posture, `RESUME_FAILED`, the save-notice contract):** every removed line of the net diff is in the test rewrite, three `Pick` types and the `Eq` pin; `FLOW_PAUSE_CAPABLE_NODE_TYPES`, `SaveNoticeConfigSchema`, the resume path and `RESUME_FAILED` are not touched. Held.
- **Load-order dependence** (the order's escalation line): resolved by ruling A and verified in ① item 6.
- **Out-of-scope findings:** #28846 (region-nested calls) correctly left out; the `#28787` skills teaching is named on the PR body's `Skills-docs` line.
- **Dogfood battery:** judged from the head's check-runs only. `Dogfood Regression Gate` is `success`; its sharded leg and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are `skipped` on this PR event. No check-run on the head reports the 4 local reds the dev attributes to 18.0-fixture pins; they are not a verdict of this head's gates and are out of this record's reach.
- **Governed surfaces:** none in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged against the published spec on `main`: `save-notice-placement.ts` (#28806) refuses what the parse can see and states in its own header that a `subflow`/`map` child's suspension is "left to the run" — this change makes that gap loud before any run, at the one gate the spec's own precedent (ADR-0126 §7.3, the disabled-subflow decline) already uses. It takes no declared capability away: the flow still registers, saves and validates; what it withholds is an arming that could only ever strand every decision.

1. **Does the trap walk hold?** Yes. Call node must be reachable from start; the notice must be reachable from the call node's successors (so a notice ahead of the call, or on a branch beside it, is not declined; a loop back from after the call is). A region-body notice is judged by its container, as in #28806. A second call node is tried when the first reaches no notice. Controls for non-suspending child, notice-ahead and cycles are pinned.
2. **Does "can suspend" hold?** It is the spec's own `FLOW_PAUSE_CAPABLE_NODE_TYPES` reachable from the child's start, else a reachable call whose child can suspend, transitively. Same deliberate limits as the parse: a plugin-registered pausing type and a region-nested call are not read (the run-time refusal by name still meets them). A child with no `start` node reads as not suspending — the same reading the spec's own `suspendedReach` takes without one; noted, not a finding.
3. **Is the verdict order-independent?** Yes (① item 6). The one asymmetry — removal does not re-judge — is declared in the PR and errs on the unarmed side.
4. **Does the status surface lie?** No. `describeUnboundReason` reports the cause only for an enabled, resolved, unbound flow, after policy and disabled-subflow (both of which outrank it, and a stale notice entry under them is recomputed the moment the gate runs past the disabled half). `getFlowRuntimeStates` carries `reason` and `unboundCause` together or not at all, as before. The warn and the reason share one sentence (`describeSubflowNoticeTrap`), name the notice, the call node, the child's suspending node (and the flow holding it when reached through further calls), and the two remedies; no tracker number in runtime text.
5. **Does the rewritten round-trip test still pin what it pinned?** Every resumed-leg pin survives unchanged in case 2: the pause row at `review` with `status: 'paused'`, the stored context without the channel's function, the child's request at `ask`, `decide` answering `resumed: true` with `resumeFailure { RESUME_FAILED, runId, 'stranded' }`, the refusal text on `resumeError` and on the terminal history row, and nothing reaching the write after the answer. What moved is how the run starts: `automation.execute` with the context the trigger hands a run, instead of the trigger itself. The one assertion dropped — the create's own answer carrying the first notice through the real trigger — is pinned in `trigger-record-change/src/record-change-integration.test.ts` (#28251 block) and `save-notice-channel.test.ts`. Case 1 now pins the decline through the real trigger (registered, `bound: false`, the right cause, a create that starts no run and hears nothing) and is the first in-composition pin of the new gate. Case 3 (#28806 refusal at `registerFlow`) is unchanged.
6. **Shipped flows.** The PR's measure (one `save_notice` in the showcase with no call node; none in the dogfood fixtures; none in hotcrm) is consistent with hotcrm `a5982564` read here (zero `save_notice` matches). No shipped flow moves.
7. **Cost.** `transitiveSubflowCallers` scans the flow map once per discovered caller; the early return on empty maps keeps the boot pull at base cost; after triggers bind it is one extra scan family per registration, same order as the existing `packagedSubflowCallers` scan.

Findings: two should-fix (the `Clause-②` arm in ②; the two stale "moved unedited" docblocks in ③). No must-fix.
